clue.text: Place very large individual in small section

indicators.note: in says the giant and the person are placed inside the abbreviated section

parts.note: DEPT is the short form of department, a section of an organisation
OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize
I is one, a single individual

explanation.surface: Someone arranges for a huge person to be seated in a little part of the hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small section' means the abbreviation of department, not a short passage.
explanation.definitionFit: To deposit something is to put it down somewhere, a synonym of setting or placing it.

clue.text: Pipes hiding Antonio's original old coins

indicators.note: hiding says the pipes enclose the opening letter of the name

parts.note: ducts are pipes or channels carrying air or fluid

indicators.note: original means the first letter of Antonio's is taken

explanation.surface: Tubes conceal the money of Antonio, the merchant in Shakespeare's Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: Antonio is Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice, a play full of ducats, so the surface sits in the right world.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducats were gold or silver pieces once used across Europe, especially Venice.

clue.text: Tree that's fashionable no longer?

indicators.note: no longer says the word for fashionable is shortened, here by losing a letter

parts.note: popular means fashionable or in vogue

explanation.surface: A tree that has fallen out of favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer' looks like 'not any more', but it means 'made shorter': drop the U, itself the crossword code for upper-class or fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: The poplar is a tall, fast-growing tree of the willow family.

clue.text: Unlikely to stumble, but refuse to do otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise says the letters of refuse to do are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A careful walker will not trip because they decline to act any other way.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is steady on their feet rarely trips or falls.

clue.text: Capricorn perhaps lacks right subject

indicators.note: lacks says a letter is taken out of the line of latitude

parts.note: the Tropic of Capricorn is one example of a tropic

explanation.surface: A goat-sign astrology column lacks the right theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the theme or matter under discussion.

clue.text: Quietly slipped into saint's memorial with a copy

indicators.note: slipped into says the soft letter is tucked inside the holy keepsake

parts.note: a relic is a bone or object kept in memory of a saint
P is piano, the musical direction for playing softly

explanation.surface: Something is discreetly placed in a shrine alongside a duplicate.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact reproduction, a synonym of a copy.

clue.text: Equipment and morale destroyed in a rambling performance

parts.note: a rig is gear or equipment

indicators.note: destroyed says the letters of morale are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Gear failure and shattered spirits ruin a long-winded show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' makes AROLE; 'in' links. 'a rambling performance' looks like the scene the gear failure ruins, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, confused procedure or tale.

clue.text: Fruit and veg starting to rot

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable

indicators.note: starting to says only the opening letter of rot is used

explanation.surface: Fruit and vegetables are beginning to go bad.
explanation.definitionFit: The pear is an orchard fruit from the apple family.

clue.text: Daring to cook tripe in dahl for starter

indicators.note: to cook says the letters of tripe in are mixed up
for starter means the first letter of dahl is taken

explanation.surface: It is bold to cook offal in a lentil dish as the first course.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means fearless or bold, a synonym of daring.

clue.text: A night out across the city? Whatever

indicators.note: across says the scrambled letters go round the abbreviation for the city
out says the letters of A night are jumbled

parts.note: NY is New York, the city

explanation.surface: Someone is indifferent to where they spend a night out on the town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' makes ATHING from A NIGHT, and 'across' puts it around NY after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean any thing at all, an indifferent reply showing no preference.

clue.text: Primate trapped by credit scam

indicators.note: trapped by says the monkey sits inside the abbreviation for credit

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A monkey is caught out by a fraudulent credit trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is slang for a crime or dodgy scheme, close to a scam or swindle.

clue.text: Display seniority in the storeroom

indicators.note: in says the years of seniority go inside the food cupboard

parts.note: a pantry is a small room for storing food
age brings seniority, being older

explanation.surface: Someone shows off how senior they are by standing in the larder.
explanation.definitionFit: Pageantry is elaborate ceremonial show, a grand display or spectacle.

clue.text: Trade barrier on the way

parts.note: read as economics it is a tariff; read cryptically, trade is another word for road vehicles moving, and a barrier to them on the road is a hold-up of cars

explanation.surface: A tariff obstacle is about to come into force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trade barrier' suggests a tariff or embargo; 'traffic' also means trade, and 'on the way' points to the road rather than the future.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailback of vehicles blocks movement along a road, so it is literally an obstruction on the highway.

clue.text: Engage in some shenanigans

indicators.note: in says the answer lies inside the words some shenanigans

explanation.surface: Someone is invited to take part in a little mischief.
explanation.definitionFit: Gears mesh when their teeth interlock, which is what engaging means in mechanics.

clue.text: It's all over for the extended banquet

parts.note: wide means extended or broad
a spread is a lavish meal laid out

explanation.surface: The party is finished for a long feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's all over' reads as 'finished'; here 'all over' means everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Something found everywhere is extensive or prevalent.

clue.text: European attitude to lead

parts.note: a Pole is a person from Poland, a European
a position is a stance or attitude on an issue

explanation.surface: A man from Europe adopts a particular stance in order to take charge.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing this is the front place on the starting grid, the leading spot.

clue.text: Designated organ and corrected faults

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing
a teacher who marks work picks out and corrects its mistakes

explanation.surface: A musical instrument has been repaired and assigned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the musical instrument but is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Earmarked means set aside or assigned for a particular purpose.

clue.text: Counsellors these days face protection

parts.note: AD (anno Domini) marks the present era
visors are shields worn over the face

explanation.surface: Modern advisers come up against protection measures.
explanation.definitionFit: Advisors give counsel, so they are guides or counsellors.

clue.text: Identifies and develops oil asset

indicators.note: develops says the letters of oil asset are worked into something new

explanation.surface: An oil company spots and exploits a resource.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate something is to single it out, as a chemist picks out a compound.

clue.text: Upset, she denied art was constructive

indicators.note: was constructive says the letters of she denied art are built into a new shape

explanation.surface: A woman upset an artist by refusing to accept that art can be constructive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was constructive' is read as 'got constructed', rebuilding the letters of SHE DENIED ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has lost heart is dispirited, a meaning of upset.

clue.text: Party like this needs agents — and luck to start

parts.note: so means thus or like this
the CIA is the American intelligence agency, staffed by agents

indicators.note: to start means only the opening letter of luck is used

explanation.surface: A gathering of this kind needs spies and a bit of luck to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is an informal party or gathering.

clue.text: Break the rules with high finish

parts.note: high food is starting to go off, smelling of decay
end means finish

explanation.surface: Someone flouts the regulations with a top-flight ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' suggests a lofty or excellent finish; here it is meat gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend is to transgress or commit a wrong against the law.

clue.text: Troubles with invoices — no heading

indicators.note: no heading says the word for invoices loses its first letter

parts.note: bills are invoices asking for payment

explanation.surface: Someone has worries about paperwork that arrives without a header.
explanation.definitionFit: Ills are misfortunes or problems, a synonym of troubles.

clue.text: Mac should dilute the strength of alcohol

parts.note: to water a drink is to dilute it
proof is the measure of how strong a spirit is

explanation.surface: Someone named Mac advises adding water to weaken a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A mac (mackintosh) is a British name for a raincoat; the capital M tempts the reader to see a Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A mac is a raincoat, a garment that keeps the rain out.

clue.text: Makes a profit from noisy vessels

indicators.note: noisy says the word for vessels is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: urns are vases or vessels

explanation.surface: A trader makes money from clattering pots.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech URNS and EARNS sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who earns money gains income or profit.

clue.text: Propose to relocate

explanation.surface: A suggestion that someone should move house.
explanation.definitionFit: To move a motion is to put it forward formally; to move house is to change where you live.

clue.text: Employee on strike? No, just not in the office

definitions.text: Employee on strike? No, just not in the office

parts.words: Employee on strike? No, just not in the office
parts.note: the phrase for a striker is someone who is out; here the worker is out only in the sense of working from home or off-site

explanation.surface: A colleague is absent, but it turns out they are not on strike, merely working elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On strike' leads to a picket line; the clue then corrects itself to someone who simply works away from the employer's premises.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of staff member does their job at home or off the premises rather than at the firm's base.

clue.text: The best part of the hotel, it emerges

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: It turns out the finest area is part of the hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the pick of a group, its finest members.

clue.text: Southern states writer died with hang over

parts.note: US is the United States
a pen is a writing implement
D is the genealogical abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A Southern American author dies after a hangover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hang over' looks like 'hangover'; 'over' just says the wordplay comes before the definition 'hang'.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to hang it from above.

clue.text: Tot in toboggan prepared for a ride

indicators.note: in says the summing word goes inside the sledge

parts.note: a sled is a toboggan
to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: A small child on a sledge is made ready for a trip downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a small child; here it is the verb meaning to add up.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that has been saddled has had its seat fitted, ready to be ridden.
